title: Hazel and the Clock
premise: In the winter of 1743, Beatrix Thornbury, apprentice to the late mapmaker Aldous Wren, must complete his final atlas before the river ice breaks and the flood season claims the low-lying workshop district. A sealed letter hidden in the clock of the workshop reveals that Wren was murdered for the atlas, which charts a smugglers' route the powerful Corvane family will do anything to bury. Hunted and abandoned by the guild that should protect her, Beatrix races to finish the plates while deciding whether to destroy the dangerous map or publish it and inherit Wren's enemies. She chooses truth, publishing the atlas as the river breaks its banks, and in the flood's aftermath the Corvanes fall and Beatrix claims the workshop as her own.
about_author: Elodie Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing eighteenth-century trade maps before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted boathouse, where the river's moods dictate her working hours.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Clock
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Alone in Wren's frozen workshop, Beatrix works by candlelight to finish his atlas when the mantel clock jams and yields a sealed letter naming the Corvane family and warning that the atlas must never be finished. She dismisses it as her master's paranoia until she finds his survey notes tampered with. Emotional beat: dread creeping into devotion.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, with an interlude in Wren's old journal. Following the letter's clues, she discovers the atlas's final plate charts a smugglers' route the Corvanes used to move contraband and people, and that Wren's 'accidental' death was no accident. A Corvane agent visits the workshop with a generous offer to buy it outright. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Ink Before Icebreak
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Refusing to sell, Beatrix enlists a disgraced guild engraver, Tomas, to help her complete and hide duplicate plates as the Corvanes escalate from threats to arson. The guild revokes her apprenticeship, leaving her legally nothing, and Tomas urges flight; she chooses to stay and finish. Emotional beat: love and loyalty tested against survival.

chapters.title: The Atlas Stands
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. On the night the ice breaks, the Corvanes come to burn the workshop; Beatrix triggers the flood sluices, drowning their attack as the river takes the lower district. She survives with the plates, publishes the atlas under Wren's name and her own, and the Corvanes are undone by their own mapped routes. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed—she becomes the mapmaker.
